PullRequest.Title: Implement zoom feature for WYSIWYG Markdown editor
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request implements a zoom feature for the WYSIWYG Markdown editor, allowing users to adjust the zoom level independently from other components in VS Code. 

### Changes made:
- **Zoom Functionality**: Added commands for **Zoom In**, **Zoom Out**, and **Reset Zoom** that adjust the zoom level of the editor pane between 50% and 200% in 10% increments.
- **State Management**: Implemented storage of the zoom level alongside scroll position and selection, ensuring that the zoom state is preserved across editor reloads and mode changes.
- **Rendering Adjustments**: Modified the CSS to scale the entire editor content, including text, images, and embedded elements, while maintaining correct viewport sizing and scrolling behavior.
- **Testing**: Created focused regression tests to validate the zoom functionality, ensuring that selection, reading position, and overlay placements are accurate at various zoom levels.

### Additional Notes:
- The implementation is designed to be minimal while ensuring that the zoom feature does not interfere with other editor functionalities.
- The changes have been verified through multiple tests, confirming that the zoom feature works as intended without affecting other components of the editor.

Scenarios.Scenario: Zoom the active Markdown rich-editor pane, including repeated commands while scrolled or editing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Command registration forwards to MarkdownEditorProvider.executeCommand, which awaits one renderer.command RPC. The renderer synchronously locates an anchor, changes CSS zoom, adjusts scroll, and persists the small view state. A subsequent measured-layout notification can perform one additional anchor correction; the anchor is cleared before correction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a command request to the active editor renderer and receive its response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical RPC per zoom command, independent of document blocks and number of open panes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zoom commands did not exist; other rich-editor commands already used this same one-active-pane RPC route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command awaits renderer processing; zoom does not wait for filesystem, subprocess, database, or network work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM geometry, update CSS zoom, force geometry to be current for scroll anchoring, and optionally correct once after responsive layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded number of geometry reads per effective zoom change and at most one deferred anchor consumption; browser reflow cost depends on document layout size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No pane-local zoom reflow or anchoring existed. Existing editor measurement and rendering were already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Geometry and initial scroll correction are synchronous on the renderer thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-stringify and post the persisted webview view state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate small-state save per effective zoom change, plus existing frame-throttled saves if scroll changes. State contains only scrollTop, selection offsets, and zoomPercent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selection changes and scrolling already serialized the same bounded state without the additional numeric zoom field; there was no zoom-triggered save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization is synchronous but payload size is independent of document length; delivery does not block zoom on external I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Document DOM/text size controls browser reflow cost; command frequency controls how often zoom changes. Zoom is bounded to 50–200%; commands at an unchanged value return early. Only the active pane is addressed, not all open panes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer JavaScript runs synchronously per command; there is no newly introduced per-document-item async fan-out. A single pending anchor is replaced/reused across successive commands, and scroll persistence remains requestAnimationFrame-throttled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new content cache or per-command collection is created. Existing model and DOM are reused. The pending anchor is a single Range, cleared on consumption or the next zoom operation; persisted state adds one numeric field.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the command, state-save, and bounded anchor paths from inspected source. Insufficient evidence to classify the necessary user-requested zoom reflow as an actionable regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large-document reflow time is unmeasured, and dependency-internal layout scheduling is unavailable. The additional geometry reads serve the new zoom anchoring behavior; a redundant scaling loop or unbounded command workload was not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression: work is scoped to an explicit effective zoom change, state is bounded, and no per-block boundary fan-out is added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopen or restore a zoomed pane, keep split panes independent, and switch between read and edit mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Saved view state is captured once during view construction; zoom is applied before the view is appended and before final scroll restoration. Existing model/view initialization and content connection remain on the open path. Mode changes update the existing presentation rather than recreating the view.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/markdown-language-features/markdown-editor-src/editor.ts:456 savedViewState and :501 zoom restoration; src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/pre/index.html:235 restored state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reuse the existing deserialized webview state to restore zoom.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local getState read during view construction, already present before the diff; one additional scalar is consumed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same webview state restored scroll and selection, without zoom.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional request is awaited before rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/markdown-language-features/markdown-editor-src/editor.ts:336 ready and :651 setReadonly; extensions/markdown-language-features/src/preview/markdownEditorProvider.ts:548 ready and :599 setReadonly
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing content/ready messaging and persistence of read/edit mode through the extension host global state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing ready processing per webview generation and one setReadonly request per actual post-initialization mode transition. Zoom adds no mode-persistence request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical ready and mode-persistence boundaries occurred without zoom restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Content synchronization retains its existing startup dependency; mode persistence is unchanged and is not awaited by #setZoom.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One saved zoom number per pane. Document size and existing code-block count determine baseline initialization costs. Each split pane owns its own Editor instance and webview state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: View setup is synchronous, with existing asynchronous content/highlighting and lazy embedded-editor work. Scroll restoration remains bounded to at most six animation-frame attempts. The added measurement autorun is registered for disposal with the Editor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Zoom is read from existing webview state, not from a new configuration or remote lookup. Cold opens without a saved value keep 100%; warm restoration sets a single CSS property. The diff does not modify content/provider caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in placement of restoration before DOM attachment, bounded scroll retries, disposal ownership, and absence of new configuration I/O.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings for restoring very large documents are available. The external editor's measurement implementation could not be inspected, but the diff introduces no observable repeated initialization or external lookup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: restoration adds a scalar style assignment and an owned observer, rather than a new expensive startup boundary or growing retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show suggestions and diagnostic hovers while typing, moving the pointer, scrolling, or resizing a zoomed editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Completion requests retain their existing host/provider path. Once shown, overlay layout uses a coordinate-space capture and existing bounds reads. Diagnostic pointer hit testing still scans existing marks, while hover creation retains its debounce and same-items suppression; added code converts coordinates using CSS zoom.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure overlay/editor/diagnostic DOM geometry and position existing overlays.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Constant overlay-layout reads per existing layout trigger; diagnostic geometry reads remain per rendered mark on pointer movement. The diff adds a scale read per pointer event and adjusts existing coordinate math.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same layout triggers, mark scan, hover construction, and synchronous geometry reads existed. Container bounds subtraction is replaced by coordinate-space conversion; no collection traversal or event subscription is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous renderer-thread work, but existing geometry scans and hover DOM reconstruction already occupied these paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/markdown-language-features/markdown-editor-src/completionController.ts:100 start and diagnosticsController.ts:32 refresh; src/preview/markdownEditorLanguageFeatures.ts:25 diagnostics and :30 completions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch diagnostics or a completion list from the host; completion invokes vscode.executeCompletionItemProvider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One diagnostics RPC per existing refresh trigger and one completions RPC per issued request, regardless of item count. Layout, hover positioning, and zoom commands do not call either method.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical diagnostics and completion request triggers and host calls occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion results await the existing text drain and provider command; positioning adds no request to that chain.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Diagnostic hit testing scales with rendered diagnostic marks per pointer event, as before. Suggestion data scales with one returned completion list per request, not one IPC per suggestion. New scale arithmetic is constant work per existing mark.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion scheduling keeps the existing 150ms automatic-request debounce and cancellation behavior. Overlay layout remains synchronous under autorun, ResizeObserver, scroll, and resize. Diagnostic hover display keeps its existing 300ms initial delay and same-item deduplication.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Diagnostics remain in the existing observable item array; hover.show avoids rebuilding for the same items. No new cache is introduced or invalidated. Closed suggestions return before coordinate-space capture.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged boundary cardinality, guards, debounce, and hover deduplication. No evidence that the new coordinate math materially amplifies the pre-existing expensive paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The internal implementation of coordinateSpace.capture is in an unavailable npm dependency, so its exact measurement cost cannot be established. Existing linear diagnostic hit testing is not a diff-introduced regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression: coordinate corrections alone do not prove increased expensive work, and existing mark scans/provider requests remain outside the diff's causal scope.

Scenarios.Scenario: Zoom or restore documents containing code blocks, embedded editors, comments, and rich links
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS zoom scales the existing editor subtree and overlays; #setZoom does not replace source text, recreate EditorView, refresh embedded editors, or directly invoke highlighting/link/provider RPCs. Existing rendering can relayout embedded content; lazy module/provider initialization retains its prior ownership.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing per-session syntax-highlighting RPC to computeFullSyntaxHighlighting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing code-block session creation/text-update/theme triggers; no additional request is directly issued by the changed zoom code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same syntax-session lifecycle and highlighting bridge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous baseline highlighting; zoom does not await re-highlighting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read static provider HTML resources, or activate/resolve an exported provider and read its resolved resources through the existing pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Static resource reads occur per eligible static contribution during provider loading; dynamic descriptor resolution joins the existing provider/document/language cache. No new read loop or cache invalidation is added by zoom.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider loading, promise caching, and failure/empty-result eviction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing provider setup is asynchronous; #setZoom does not await provider loading or resource reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing batched rich-link subscriptions and embedded-editor runtime transport messaging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Subscriptions are deduplicated by href and sent in microtask batches; embedded transports follow existing runtime lifetimes. The diff neither creates a per-zoom subscription batch nor directly creates transports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same subscription batching, inactive cache, runtime creation, and disposal paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by zoom; baseline rich metadata and embedded runtimes can load independently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Baseline syntax work scales with code blocks; embedded provider resolution is effectively grouped by provider/document/language through the host promise cache, not necessarily per block. Rich-link entries are deduplicated by href. Zoomed viewport geometry can change visible content, but no diff-introduced per-item recreation is evidenced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: LazyCodeBlockEditorFactory starts one module load per factory. Existing host descriptor resolution joins an in-flight promise for the same provider/document/language; distinct keys may resolve independently. Rich-link subscription changes are microtask-batched. The diff changes none of these concurrency controls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider API promises are cached per contribution; descriptor successes are cached per provider/document/language, while empty or failed descriptor results are evicted. Rich-link presentations retain reference counting and a five-minute, 256-entry inactive cache. Syntax sessions persist for existing blocks; zoom does not explicitly invalidate them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged inspected wrappers, caches, lazy-loading guard, and absence of direct zoom-to-provider calls. Lower visibility into dependency-internal resize behavior is a review limitation rather than evidence of a regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External markdown-editor layout and iframe virtualization internals are unavailable, so exact resize messaging and viewport-dependent activation cannot be quantified. No new filesystem/network/subprocess/database boundary or increased provider-resolution frequency is demonstrated by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: scaling richer existing content does not itself establish new expensive boundary fan-out, cache churn, or leaked runtime ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 11 changed files and every diff page against base 51ec2db5fb2946a1705beee4d439aa972c2e6845. Traced active-pane commands, zoom anchoring/state serialization, restoration/read-edit/split-pane lifecycle, completion/diagnostic overlays, and embedded-content boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced actionable performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix was established. Added browser tests and documentation do not introduce production runtime work. Static-source limitation: @vscode/markdown-editor npm internals were unavailable; no performance measurements were made.
